correctness.rationale: The divisor-sign construction gives a valid bipartition for every seed z=2^a p with 2^a<p<2^(a+1); coprime direct-product partition proves closure on z+z^2t. PNT bounds the least odd p∤N by 2log N for all large odd N. Then m=z²<16log^4 N and gcd(N-z,m)=1, so uniform Siegel--Walfisz gives ≥N/(4φ(m)log N) prime choices in the middle third, implying R(N)≥N/(100log^5 N). All quantifiers, signs, lower endpoints and asymptotic error bounds checked; 46 seed and 9 product finite checks are supplementary only. Ineffective N0 disclosed.

originality.rationale: The 2023 source explicitly poses complete odd coverage as Conjecture 4.20, proves only residue-restricted cases and finite checks; the 2020 source contains constructive Zumkeller ingredients but no additive prime-distribution theorem. The new varying-modulus argument using p(N)≤2log N and uniform Siegel--Walfisz yields a quantitative bound covering every sufficiently large odd N, which is not implied by those statements. Three direct mathematical-claim searches and database comparisons returned no covering result; non-exhaustive indexing is a residual risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or inaccessible later work might contain an equivalent Siegel--Walfisz application.
The full 2013 Peng--Bhaskara Rao journal article was not inspected; however the needed closure step is reproved directly and the accessible later source explicitly identifies it as known.
An inequality for finitely many small odd N is not established; the theorem is only eventual and ineffective.

value.rationale: The 2023 originating paper explicitly conjectures prime-plus-Zumkeller coverage for all odd integers greater than eight except 21, and its existing congruence argument omits infinitely many odd inputs. Establishing existence for every sufficiently large odd N and a growing quantitative number of distinct representations gives a motivated partial resolution of that published problem and a new uniformity phenomenon rather than a routine exercise or an arbitrary cutoff.
